- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

# Clean design specification
Ethereum NFT raffle; immutable factory, ERC-1167 clones with immutable implementation. One entry costs 1,000,000 units of canonical six-decimal USDC. One purchase mints a transferable ERC721 ticket representing a contiguous inclusive range. Exactly one ERC721 prize is escrowed atomically at creation. Reserve met awards NFT and 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refund outcome pays 100% per entry and returns prize. Rounding is floor on aggregate protocol fee; remainder must be allocated without loss. No administrator, mutable configuration or upgrade. Request window [sale end, end+2days); callback accepted strictly before request timestamp+2days. Refunds open at deadline. Callback records result only. Settlement is permissionless, storage-only; redemption requires current ticket owner, burns claim atomically, and must revert all effects on delivery failure. Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement. Never move assets between raffle clones. Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies; arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted. Frontend discovery is advisory; transaction decisions must reread current chain state.

This specification was composed before scanner results and historical findings. Source, not design prose, determines actual behavior. No tests, audit history, accepted-risk lists or scanner results are provided.

7	/// @dev The factory has no owner, pause, upgrade, rescue, or mutable protocol configuration. Deployment tooling must

11	interface IRaffleFactory {

13	
14	    /// @notice Sponsor-selected configuration for one new raffle.
15	    /// @param sponsorRecipient Immutable recipient of sponsor quote proceeds and any returned prize.
16	    /// @param prizeToken Standards-compliant ERC-721 prize contract.
17	    /// @param prizeTokenId Token ID to escrow atomically during creation.
18	    /// @param reserveEntries Global raw entry-count threshold selecting the NFT outcome when met or exceeded.

32	    /// @param raffle Newly created fixed-target ERC-1167 clone.
33	    /// @param sponsor Prize depositor and pre-end empty-raffle refund authority.
34	    /// @param sponsorRecipient Immutable recipient of sponsor quote proceeds and any returned prize.
35	    /// @param prizeToken ERC-721 contract of the escrowed prize.

modules.name: RaffleFactory
modules.role: Ownerless factory with no admin, pause, upgrade or rescue. The constructor fixes quoteToken (checked only for code and decimals()==6), vrfWrapper (checked only for code) and protocolTreasury (screened against self, quote, wrapper and implementation), then deploys the single Raffle implementation, whose constructor captures factory=msg.sender. createRaffle validates the sponsor's params, ERC-1167-clones the implementation (CREATE) and initializes the clone. It then writes the raffleById/idByRaffle/isRaffle registry and pulls the prize with prize.safeTransferFrom(sponsor, clone, id), verifying prize.ownerOf==clone and clone.status()==Active. Every clone reads the registry (isRaffle, raffleImplementation) to screen destinations.

modules.name: Raffle
modules.role: Per-raffle ERC-1167 clone (614 lines). It combines four things. (1) Escrow of one prize NFT. (2) USDC accounting in five buckets: unsettledPot, remainingRefundLiability, winnerProceeds, sponsorProceeds and protocolFees. (3) The 'raffle.fun Ticket' ERC-721, with one sequential ticket per purchase holding an inclusive uint128 entry range. (4) A Chainlink VRF v2.5 native-payment wrapper consumer. Lifecycle: AwaitingPrize -> Active -> Drawing -> NftWon|CashWon, plus Active|Drawing -> Refunding on timeouts. The constructor locks the implementation's own storage (initialized=true, status=Refunding). User-facing mutators are nonReentrant, except initialize, onERC721Received, inherited rawFulfillRandomWords and the inherited ERC721 transfer/approval functions. Unrelated NFTs sent with plain transferFrom stay stuck by design (documented). USDC accounting uses nominal amounts with no balance-delta checks.

modules.name: IRaffle
modules.role: Raffle ABI: Status enum, RaffleInitParams struct, events, custom errors and NatSpec pre/postconditions. No logic. The NatSpec states trust assumptions: the quote token is canonical USDC with standard, non-rebasing, fee-free transfers, and 'Supported prizes are honest, standards-compliant ERC-721s'. This differs from DESIGN.md, which treats arbitrary prize contracts as untrusted.

modules.name: IRaffleFactory
modules.role: Factory ABI: CreateRaffleParams (sponsorRecipient, prizeToken, prizeTokenId, reserveEntries, endTime), RaffleCreated event, errors, and the registry/config getters that clones call during screening. No logic. The NatSpec says deployment tooling must verify the canonical USDC address because on-chain checks are limited to code and decimals.

modules.name: RaffleConstants
modules.role: Fixed v1 economics, timing and limits: BPS=10_000, PROTOCOL_FEE_BPS=500, CASH_WINNER_BPS=8000, ENTRY_PRICE=1_000_000, QUOTE_TOKEN_DECIMALS=6, MAX_REFUND_TICKET_BATCH_SIZE=100, MAX_SALE_DURATION=30 days, DRAW_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=2 days, DRAW_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT=2 days, VRF_CALLBACK_GAS_LIMIT=300_000, VRF_REQUEST_CONFIRMATIONS=30. Because gross is always a multiple of 1e6, the 5% and 80% mulDiv results come out exact.

modules.name: Inherited OpenZeppelin 5.6.1 (ERC721, ERC721Utils, ReentrancyGuard, SafeERC20, Math, Clones)
modules.role: Not in src, but part of the deployed ABI and behavior. ERC721 provides public transferFrom, safeTransferFrom (two overloads), approve and setApprovalForAll with no reentrancy guard; all ticket mints, transfers and burns go through the Raffle._update override. _safeMint and safeTransferFrom call the recipient's onERC721Received. ReentrancyGuard is storage-based at the ERC-7201 slot 0x9b779b17...5f00. Fresh clones hold 0 there, which counts as not-entered because the check is ==ENTERED(2). Math.mulDiv rounds down. Clones.clone uses CREATE.

modules.name: Inherited Chainlink VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase (@chainlink/contracts 1.5.0)
modules.role: Provides the immutables i_vrfV2PlusWrapper and i_linkToken (its constructor calls wrapper.link()). It also provides external rawFulfillRandomWords, whose only authentication is msg.sender==wrapper before dispatching to Raffle.fulfillRandomWords; it has no reentrancy guard. Its internal requestRandomnessPayInNative re-quotes calculateRequestPriceNative and forwards exactly that value. It also exposes the getBalance and getLinkToken views.

candidates.name: Raffle.redeemWinningTicket (L309-346)
candidates.why: Only path that delivers the main prize. Checks winnerRedeemed and NftWon/CashWon, settles inline or requires ticketId==winningTicketId, requires ownerOf==msg.sender, records the winner and burns, then sends the NFT (untrusted prizeToken.transferFrom + ownerOf check) or the cash (_transferQuote). The design requires every effect to revert if delivery fails.

candidates.name: Raffle._settleWinningTicket (L533-558), reached via settleWinningTicket L304 and redeemWinningTicket
candidates.why: Permissionless, one-shot split of the whole unsettledPot into protocolFees (5%, rounded down), winnerProceeds (80%, rounded down, CashWon only) and sponsorProceeds (the remainder); sets settlementComplete/winningTicketId and zeroes the pot. Conservation and the 95/5 vs 80/15/5 splits depend on this function.

candidates.name: Raffle.buyEntries (L209-237)
candidates.why: Only USDC inflow and only ticket mint. Checks status, time, recipient, count>0 and uint128 headroom; credits the nominal amount with no balance-delta check (fee-free token assumption); assigns the next contiguous range and bumps the counters and unsettledPot; then _safeMint calls the untrusted recipient. The range-partition invariant starts here.

candidates.name: Raffle.refundTickets (L349-372)
candidates.why: Untrusted array of 1-100 IDs during Refunding. Per ID: owner check (ownerOf reverts on burned or nonexistent tickets, which also rejects duplicates), range sum, burn. The total is debited from remainingRefundLiability (checked) and paid to msg.sender. Conservation assumes the ranges partition [1,totalEntries].

candidates.name: Raffle.enableRefunds (L276-301)
candidates.why: Terminal move to Refunding with three deadline cases (empty Active: sponsor any time, others at endTime; sold Active: endTime+2d; Drawing: drawRequestedAt+2d) that moves unsettledPot into remainingRefundLiability. These >= boundaries must not overlap the < windows of buyEntries, requestDraw and callback acceptance.

candidates.name: Raffle.fulfillRandomWords (L509-524), reached via inherited rawFulfillRandomWords
candidates.why: Decides the winner and outcome. Silently ignores in-flight, non-Drawing, wrong-ID, wrong-length or late callbacks; otherwise sets winningEntry = word % totalEntries + 1 and status NftWon if totalEntries >= reserveEntries, else CashWon. Relies on totalEntries being frozen after endTime and on wrapper authentication.

candidates.name: Raffle.requestDraw (L240-273)
candidates.why: Payable, permissionless move from Active to Drawing in [endTime, endTime+2d) when totalEntries>0. Checks msg.value against the quote; sets status, drawRequestedAt and _requestInFlight before the trusted wrapper call; records vrfRequestId; then refunds msg.value-paidPrice to msg.sender through a full-gas low-level call while the guard is held.

candidates.name: RaffleFactory.createRaffle (L97-148)
candidates.why: Untrusted sponsor entry. Checks 0 < endTime-now <= 30d, bumps raffleCount, clones, initializes and registers the clone in isRaffle, then calls the untrusted prize.safeTransferFrom. Escrow is verified by prize.ownerOf==clone and status()==Active, and both checks depend on how the prize contract behaves.

candidates.name: Raffle.onERC721Received (L416-431)
candidates.why: The only move from AwaitingPrize to Active, and the clone's side of escrow verification. No reentrancy guard. Checks msg.sender==prizeToken, tokenId, from==sponsor and operator==factory, but the sponsor-chosen prize contract supplies all of those argument values.

candidates.name: Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize (L395-407)
candidates.why: Permissionless return of the NFT to sponsorRecipient in CashWon or Refunding. It is kept exclusive with winner delivery by status plus the shared prizeClaimed flag. Calls the untrusted transferFrom/ownerOf. The recipient is screened only at creation/initialize, not at release.

candidates.name: Raffle._update override (L497-502) with inherited ERC721 transferFrom/safeTransferFrom/_safeMint/_burn
candidates.why: Runs on every ticket mint, transfer and burn: screens non-zero recipients via _isProtocolDestination (factory reads), then OZ authorization and balance updates. The transfer and approval entrypoints have no reentrancy guard and stay callable inside other functions' untrusted callbacks. Refund and redemption rights follow the resulting ownerOf.

candidates.name: Raffle._isProtocolDestination (L593-605)
candidates.why: Shared denylist for initialize, ticket recipients and every USDC payout: this clone, factory, quoteToken, wrapper, prizeToken, implementation, and registered raffles. isRaffle is queried only if the address has code at call time, so the result can change as clones deploy.

candidates.name: Raffle.initialize (L176-206)
candidates.why: Factory-only, write-once clone config. Screens sponsor, protocolTreasury and sponsorRecipient (none may equal prizeToken), but relies on the factory for the prize's ERC-721 support, reserveEntries>0 and endTime bounds without rechecking them. The implementation stays locked only because its constructor set initialized=true.

candidates.name: Raffle._transferQuote (L564-567)
candidates.why: Every USDC outflow (refunds, winner cash, sponsor, treasury) passes here: the recipient is re-screened against the current registry, then SafeERC20.safeTransfer runs. Whether a payout can complete depends on the screening result at that time and the trusted token accepting the transfer.

candidates.name: Raffle._requireWinningTicket (L579-585)
candidates.why: Range check firstEntry <= winningEntry <= lastEntry. Exactly one ticket can pass because ranges are contiguous and disjoint and unminted IDs read (0,0) while winningEntry >= 1. Ranges are kept after a burn.

candidates.name: Raffle.releaseSponsorProceeds (L375-382)
candidates.why: Permissionless: zeroes sponsorProceeds, then pushes it to the immutable sponsorRecipient through _transferQuote. Independent of the fee release; non-zero only after settlement.

candidates.name: Raffle.releaseProtocolFees (L385-392)
candidates.why: Permissionless: zeroes protocolFees, then pushes it to the immutable protocolTreasury through _transferQuote. Independent of the sponsor release; non-zero only after settlement.

candidates.name: RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams (L154-179)
candidates.why: Checks sponsor input. prizeToken must have code, must not be factory, quote, wrapper, implementation or a registered raffle, and must report ERC-721 via try/catch supportsInterface on untrusted code. sponsorRecipient must be non-zero and not protocol plumbing or the prize token. reserveEntries must be > 0.

candidates.name: VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.rawFulfillRandomWords (Chainlink L101-107)
candidates.why: The only authentication of randomness: msg.sender must equal the immutable i_vrfV2PlusWrapper. External, with no reentrancy guard. Calldata that fails ABI decoding reverts before Raffle's ignore logic runs.

candidates.name: Raffle constructor (L155-166) and _validatedVrfWrapper (L610-613)
candidates.why: Sets the immutables every clone runs with (factory=msg.sender, quoteToken, wrapper, link token via wrapper.link()) and locks the implementation's own storage (initialized=true, status=Refunding). Clones start with zeroed storage, so before initialize their status is AwaitingPrize.

candidates.name: RaffleFactory constructor (L65-92)
candidates.why: One-time trust anchor. The quote token is checked only for code and decimals()==6, the wrapper only for code; the treasury is screened against self, quote, wrapper and implementation. Deploys the implementation. Using the canonical addresses is a tooling assumption not enforced on-chain.

candidates.name: Raffle.callbackDeadline (L463-465)
candidates.why: Returns drawRequestedAt+2d, or 0 before any request. The same value is the exclusive acceptance bound in fulfillRandomWords and the inclusive start of Drawing-case enableRefunds.

candidates.name: Raffle.drawRequestDeadline (L458-460)
candidates.why: The endTime+2d boundary shared by requestDraw (must be before it) and the sold-case enableRefunds (at or after it).

candidates.name: VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.requestRandomnessPayInNative (Chainlink L76-87)
candidates.why: Re-quotes calculateRequestPriceNative separately from requestDraw's pre-check and sends exactly that value from the clone's balance. The price it returns drives requestDraw's excess-refund arithmetic.

modules.name: RaffleFactory
modules.role: Ownerless factory with no admin, pause, upgrade or rescue. The constructor fixes quoteToken (checked only for code and decimals()==6), vrfWrapper (checked only for code) and protocolTreasury (screened against self, quote, wrapper and implementation), then deploys the single Raffle implementation, whose constructor captures factory=msg.sender. createRaffle validates the sponsor's params, ERC-1167-clones the implementation (CREATE) and initializes the clone. It then writes the raffleById/idByRaffle/isRaffle registry and pulls the prize with prize.safeTransferFrom(sponsor, clone, id), verifying prize.ownerOf==clone and clone.status()==Active. Every clone reads the registry (isRaffle, raffleImplementation) to screen destinations.

modules.name: Raffle
modules.role: Per-raffle ERC-1167 clone (614 lines). It combines four things. (1) Escrow of one prize NFT. (2) USDC accounting in five buckets: unsettledPot, remainingRefundLiability, winnerProceeds, sponsorProceeds and protocolFees. (3) The 'raffle.fun Ticket' ERC-721, with one sequential ticket per purchase holding an inclusive uint128 entry range. (4) A Chainlink VRF v2.5 native-payment wrapper consumer. Lifecycle: AwaitingPrize -> Active -> Drawing -> NftWon|CashWon, plus Active|Drawing -> Refunding on timeouts. The constructor locks the implementation's own storage (initialized=true, status=Refunding). User-facing mutators are nonReentrant, except initialize, onERC721Received, inherited rawFulfillRandomWords and the inherited ERC721 transfer/approval functions. Unrelated NFTs sent with plain transferFrom stay stuck by design (documented). USDC accounting uses nominal amounts with no balance-delta checks.

modules.name: IRaffle
modules.role: Raffle ABI: Status enum, RaffleInitParams struct, events, custom errors and NatSpec pre/postconditions. No logic. The NatSpec states trust assumptions: the quote token is canonical USDC with standard, non-rebasing, fee-free transfers, and 'Supported prizes are honest, standards-compliant ERC-721s'. This differs from DESIGN.md, which treats arbitrary prize contracts as untrusted.

modules.name: IRaffleFactory
modules.role: Factory ABI: CreateRaffleParams (sponsorRecipient, prizeToken, prizeTokenId, reserveEntries, endTime), RaffleCreated event, errors, and the registry/config getters that clones call during screening. No logic. The NatSpec says deployment tooling must verify the canonical USDC address because on-chain checks are limited to code and decimals.

modules.name: RaffleConstants
modules.role: Fixed v1 economics, timing and limits: BPS=10_000, PROTOCOL_FEE_BPS=500, CASH_WINNER_BPS=8000, ENTRY_PRICE=1_000_000, QUOTE_TOKEN_DECIMALS=6, MAX_REFUND_TICKET_BATCH_SIZE=100, MAX_SALE_DURATION=30 days, DRAW_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=2 days, DRAW_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT=2 days, VRF_CALLBACK_GAS_LIMIT=300_000, VRF_REQUEST_CONFIRMATIONS=30. Because gross is always a multiple of 1e6, the 5% and 80% mulDiv results come out exact.

modules.name: Inherited OpenZeppelin 5.6.1 (ERC721, ERC721Utils, ReentrancyGuard, SafeERC20, Math, Clones)
modules.role: Not in src, but part of the deployed ABI and behavior. ERC721 provides public transferFrom, safeTransferFrom (two overloads), approve and setApprovalForAll with no reentrancy guard; all ticket mints, transfers and burns go through the Raffle._update override. _safeMint and safeTransferFrom call the recipient's onERC721Received. ReentrancyGuard is storage-based at the ERC-7201 slot 0x9b779b17...5f00. Fresh clones hold 0 there, which counts as not-entered because the check is ==ENTERED(2). Math.mulDiv rounds down. Clones.clone uses CREATE.

modules.name: Inherited Chainlink VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase (@chainlink/contracts 1.5.0)
modules.role: Provides the immutables i_vrfV2PlusWrapper and i_linkToken (its constructor calls wrapper.link()). It also provides external rawFulfillRandomWords, whose only authentication is msg.sender==wrapper before dispatching to Raffle.fulfillRandomWords; it has no reentrancy guard. Its internal requestRandomnessPayInNative re-quotes calculateRequestPriceNative and forwards exactly that value. It also exposes the getBalance and getLinkToken views.

modules.name: RaffleFactory
modules.role: Ownerless factory with no admin, pause, upgrade or rescue. The constructor fixes quoteToken (checked only for code and decimals()==6), vrfWrapper (checked only for code) and protocolTreasury (screened against self, quote, wrapper and implementation), then deploys the single Raffle implementation, whose constructor captures factory=msg.sender. createRaffle validates the sponsor's params, ERC-1167-clones the implementation (CREATE) and initializes the clone. It then writes the raffleById/idByRaffle/isRaffle registry and pulls the prize with prize.safeTransferFrom(sponsor, clone, id), verifying prize.ownerOf==clone and clone.status()==Active. Every clone reads the registry (isRaffle, raffleImplementation) to screen destinations.

modules.name: Raffle
modules.role: Per-raffle ERC-1167 clone (614 lines). It combines four things. (1) Escrow of one prize NFT. (2) USDC accounting in five buckets: unsettledPot, remainingRefundLiability, winnerProceeds, sponsorProceeds and protocolFees. (3) The 'raffle.fun Ticket' ERC-721, with one sequential ticket per purchase holding an inclusive uint128 entry range. (4) A Chainlink VRF v2.5 native-payment wrapper consumer. Lifecycle: AwaitingPrize -> Active -> Drawing -> NftWon|CashWon, plus Active|Drawing -> Refunding on timeouts. The constructor locks the implementation's own storage (initialized=true, status=Refunding). User-facing mutators are nonReentrant, except initialize, onERC721Received, inherited rawFulfillRandomWords and the inherited ERC721 transfer/approval functions. Unrelated NFTs sent with plain transferFrom stay stuck by design (documented). USDC accounting uses nominal amounts with no balance-delta checks.

modules.name: IRaffle
modules.role: Raffle ABI: Status enum, RaffleInitParams struct, events, custom errors and NatSpec pre/postconditions. No logic. The NatSpec states trust assumptions: the quote token is canonical USDC with standard, non-rebasing, fee-free transfers, and 'Supported prizes are honest, standards-compliant ERC-721s'. This differs from DESIGN.md, which treats arbitrary prize contracts as untrusted.

modules.name: IRaffleFactory
modules.role: Factory ABI: CreateRaffleParams (sponsorRecipient, prizeToken, prizeTokenId, reserveEntries, endTime), RaffleCreated event, errors, and the registry/config getters that clones call during screening.
